Finite sums of products of individual continuous nonroot-coordinate functions form an explicit unital real subalgebra. Their append and multiplication operations are proved exactly, with the multiplication realized by a finite term expansion.

Every compact observable family has a finite uniform recipe set at each accuracy and a common finite coefficient-mass bound. Any fixed sup-bounded, fixed-Lipschitz observable family has a compact hull by a proved Arzela--Ascoli application, so the same finite recipe conclusion holds uniformly for the entire family.

A unique missing root on a genuine compact full-cube set gives an injective deletion map. Its compact-to-Hausdorff embedding has a continuous inverse onto the admissible partial-cube image, proving exact continuous missing-root reconstruction.

The triangular upper-face lattice-recovery argument is proved for arbitrary groups and arbitrary lattice subgroups without normality or commutativity. Proper face values in the lattice force each ordered face coefficient into the lattice and consequently the missing top vertex into the lattice.

For a cube subgroup with an explicit proper upper-face coordinate certificate, two quotient cubes agreeing at the proper vertices also agree at the missing top. The proved certificate-based uniqueness is connected directly to continuous reconstruction and normalized bounded-Lipschitz observable recipes, with actual cube compactness retained as an explicit hypothesis.

The actual upper-face generated cube subgroup is defined by subgroup closure of the original filtration-level face arrays. Every linear orbit cube g^(b0+sum_E bj)*x belongs to this subgroup whenever filtration levels zero and one are the whole group; translating elements, base points and all integer exponents are unrestricted.

The finite uniform recipe theorem is combined across an arbitrary fixed finite list of distinct compact ambient cube spaces and distinct bounded-Lipschitz observable families, with a single common finite coefficient bound for the whole list.

The uniformity result quantifies over the complete observable family, not just a selected finite list of observables. Arzela--Ascoli yields a compact hull; a finite uniform net plus each-center Stone--Weierstrass recipe proves the result. The common coefficient bound is independent of the observable and of the cube/base point/translation.

Normalization leaves the finite recipe exactly equal everywhere, and bounds every coordinate factor globally by one. These factors are continuous; a Lipschitz refinement of the factors themselves is not yet asserted. The observables being approximated do have the stated fixed Lipschitz bounds.

The lattice-recovery proof uses a finite ordered product in a possibly noncommutative group. Later faces do not affect earlier vertices; after recovering each coefficient, multiplying a remaining vertex by the inverse of a lattice prefix keeps it in the subgroup. No passage to a quotient group structure or subgroup normality is used.

The certificate-based result assumes explicit proper upper-face factorization of every element of the cube subgroup and actual compactness of its quotient cube image. Derivation of those inputs for the rational nilpotent Lie cube group remains required. The certificate is an explicit algebraic representation premise, not an additional axiom or an assertion that the actual cube group already satisfies it.

The independently proved linear-orbit membership uses only the actual constant and singleton face generators at filtration levels zero and one. It holds for arbitrary g, x and integer b0,bj without boundedness, commutativity of the ambient group or a nilpotence premise.

The extra zero-prime dual-template implementation was reviewed and does use the actual master modulus M; it was not replaced by a primorial-only cube. Piece-selection inputs and weighted boundaries have not yet been constructed in this round.
